title: Ohio's 2nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Ohio's 2nd Congressional District is being contested in the 2026 general election following the May 5 primary. Incumbent Republican Rep. David Taylor, first elected in 2024, faces Democratic nominee Jen Mazzuckelli. The district was redrawn in October 2025 under Ohio's mid-decade redistricting and covers a large swath of southern Ohio from Clermont County east to the West Virginia border, including Appalachian counties. The district is heavily Republican according to the Cook Partisan Voting Index, making this a race where the incumbent is strongly favored.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the OH-02 general election as of the research date. The district is considered safely Republican, and polling in this race has been minimal.

candidates.name: David J. Taylor
candidates.summary: David J. Taylor is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A former assistant prosecutor in Clermont County and president of his family's concrete business, Taylor serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure and Agriculture Committees and co-chairs the Congressional Rural Broadband Caucus. Taylor has emphasized conservative values, rural infrastructure, broadband expansion, and supporting agriculture during his first term.

candidates.name: Jen Mazzuckelli
candidates.summary: Jen Mazzuckelli is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 2nd Congressional District, having won the May 5, 2026 primary against Todd Wilson. She is a former high school English teacher and single mother from Clermont County who previously ran for county commissioner in 2024. Mazzuckelli has emphasized her background as a 'regular person' who has experienced housing and food insecurity, and she advocates for getting money out of politics, affordable housing, and mental health resources.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for OH-02, so this forecast relies entirely on structural indicators. The district is explicitly described as heavily Republican per the Cook Partisan Voting Index even after the October 2025 redistricting, covering rural southern and Appalachian counties that are strongly Republican terrain. Incumbent Rep. David J. Taylor benefits from first-term incumbency and represents a district whose partisan baseline overwhelms the Democratic challenge. Democrat Jen Mazzuckelli is a former high school teacher whose only prior electoral run (2024 county commissioner) yielded about 30% of the vote, providing no countervailing signal to the district's Republican lean. With zero polling, confidence is tempered to medium — the district fundamentals strongly support a safe Republican outcome, but direct voter-intent data is absent, introducing non-quantifiable uncertainty around the precise margin and probability estimates.
